nodes.rationale: Reports which changed lines tests execute; each change gets High/Medium/Low confidence with its rule and source URL; untested paths are Low.

nodes.label: sqlalchemy_notes fixture
nodes.rationale: Uses APIs removed in 2.0 (engine.execute, raw SQL strings, select([...]), string row keys, library-level autocommit).

nodes.label: Bumpless
nodes.rationale: Dependabot bumps the version; Bumpless makes it pass. Migrates repo code across major dependency bumps with evidence (rules, sources, tests, coverage).

nodes.label: Partial->Failed Relabel Fix (845a186259)
nodes.rationale: Status logic counted a passing generated behavior test as progress; fixed 2026-10-28.

nodes.label: Edit Guardrails
nodes.rationale: Reject edits that weaken tests, drop assertions, skip tests or stop tests calling repo code.

nodes.label: Reasoning Off (enable_thinking=false)
nodes.rationale: Nano/Super burned their 16k-token budget thinking; turning reasoning off cut research 236 s -> 137 s and tiered median run time 286 s -> 134 s.

nodes.label: Source Verification of Rules
nodes.rationale: Deterministic check that the page names the API, then Nano confirms support and that old usage really breaks; only verified, required rules are applied (optional 'new style' rules broke working SQLAlchemy code).

nodes.label: Tiered Model Routing (Nano -> Super -> Ultra)
nodes.rationale: Each task goes to the cheapest tier that does it well; failed edits escalate one tier at a time. Cheaper in every comparison (4-28% Token Factory, 29% free tier) but savings are smaller than per-token prices suggest because Ultra repair dominates cost.

nodes.label: SEARCH/REPLACE Edit Block (RULE_ID)
nodes.rationale: Each edit block cites the rule it follows (or NONE/LEARNED) so every change is traceable to a source.

nodes.label: Plan JSON (files, rule_ids, risk, notes, manual_review)
nodes.norm_label: plan json (files, rule_ids, risk, notes, manual_review)

nodes.label: Hosted Demo (bumpless.onrender.com, replays only)
nodes.rationale: Container runs EXECUTOR=local and only bundled fixtures live, never user repos; DEMO_PASSWORD and DEMO_DAILY_BUDGET_USD cap abuse and spend.

nodes.label: bumpless doctor (tier ping)
nodes.rationale: Listing a model in /v1/models is not proof it can be called, so each tier is pinged.

nodes.label: Bumpless
nodes.rationale: Dependabot bumps the version, Bumpless makes it pass: does the migration afternoon with enough evidence for a reviewer to trust it.

nodes.label: @bumpless PR Conversation (revise/explain/revert)
nodes.rationale: Refuses outside contributors (no write access) before spending a token.

nodes.label: app/storage.py (deliberately untested)
nodes.rationale: Left untested so the report marks its changes Low confidence.

nodes.label: Diagnose/Repair Prompt
nodes.rationale: Fix every visible failure in one reply; never delete/skip tests or weaken assertions; fix code not tests.

nodes.label: Per-File Edit Prompt
nodes.rationale: Rules come from official docs so prefer them over model memory; keep behavior identical; reply NO_CHANGES if nothing to do.

nodes.label: Migration Plan Prompt
nodes.rationale: Orders files (definitions before users), assigns rule ids and risk; manual_review only for concrete non-automatable problems, not generic reminders.

nodes.label: Characterization Probe Prompt
nodes.rationale: Probe calls only the repo's own code (never the package API directly, never mocks it) with fixed offline inputs, so recordings stay valid across the version change.

nodes.label: Final Review Prompt
nodes.rationale: Checks every change follows a rule, behavior preserved, no tests weakened, no unrelated edits; returns approve/summary/concerns JSON.

nodes.label: Rulebook Synthesis Prompt
nodes.rationale: One rule per distinct change; only breaking/deprecated changes, skip optional new styles; every rule cites its SOURCE URL, preferring official migration guides; ignore same-named products.

nodes.label: Doc Page Summarize Prompt (OLD/NEW/NOTE)
nodes.rationale: Worded 'guides usually describe many changes: list every one; NONE only for no upgrade content' to avoid the NONE attractor.

nodes.label: Demo Video Script (<=3:00)
nodes.rationale: Every number said must be on screen or in benchmarks/RESULTS.md; replays labeled; only show the GitHub flow if it actually ran.

nodes.label: Characterization Test Failure Handling
nodes.rationale: Failures in tests/_bumpless/test_characterization.py mean observable behavior changed; restore old behavior, never edit tests/_bumpless, unless the change is documented and unavoidable.

nodes.label: LOOKUP Error Web Search
nodes.rationale: When an error is not explained by the rulebook, the model names an exact error message to search; edits following it cite LEARNED.

nodes.label: Rule Check: about_package / supported / required
nodes.rationale: Filters sibling products sharing the name and rules that are true but optional (old usage still works), which broke working code on SQLAlchemy.

nodes.label: Grounding Rules in Fetched Pages
nodes.rationale: Nano from memory invented pydantic v2 changes; grounding every rule in a fetched page is necessary.

nodes.label: NONE Escape-Hatch Attractor
nodes.rationale: With reasoning off, 'reply NONE if nothing applies' made Nano/Super reply NONE 8/9 times on a change-rich guide chunk; rewording gave 5/5.

nodes.label: 429 Rate-Limit Backoff (10/20/40 s)
nodes.rationale: Trial tier 429s after ~30 parallel Nano calls; SDK retries span only seconds.

nodes.label: Reasoning Off (enable_thinking=false)
nodes.rationale: Cut research step from 236 s to 137 s; avoids burning 16k-token budgets thinking about edits.

nodes.label: RULE_ID Placeholder Fix
nodes.rationale: Real-looking example ids (R001) in prompts were copied as citations; a RULE_ID placeholder fixed it.

nodes.label: True-but-Optional Rules Problem
nodes.rationale: SQLAlchemy where() vs filter_by() rule was doc-supported but only for the new style; applying it broke working code, so verification asks whether old usage really breaks.

nodes.label: Tiered Model Routing & Escalation (Nano->Super->Ultra)
nodes.rationale: Cheap model is cheap only if first attempt works; most spend went to Ultra repairs. All-Ultra mode benchmarked as more reliable.

nodes.label: tiered strategy ($0.398)
nodes.rationale: Routes requests across model tiers instead of sending all to the ultra tier; ~29% lower total cost in this benchmark.

nodes.label: Total Cost Comparison Chart (all-ultra vs tiered)
nodes.norm_label: total cost comparison chart (all-ultra vs tiered)

nodes.label: Success Rate Chart (% green)
nodes.rationale: Horizontal bar chart comparing benchmark success rate (% of runs ending green): tiered model routing reaches 100% vs all-ultra at 60%, showing tiered routing is more reliable.
